metadata.method: Review event-level sources for NCEI segment primaries, preserve IDs/alternates except specifically reselected Aug13 pair, document publisher/measurement dependence, avoid all approval inflation.

reviews.title_after: North Texas sleet and ice storm begins a multiday freeze
reviews.evidence_independence: same NOAA/NWS reporting network as NCEI segment; independently authored retrospective, not separate measured sleet observations
reviews.core_fact: On January 30, 2023, sleet and freezing rain began a multiday North and Central Texas winter-weather episode that continued into February 1; the NCEI Tarrant County record is a local event segment.
reviews.unverified_claims: Do not attribute all airport cancellations to January 30 alone; the event lasted through February 1 and travel disruptions through February 3. County sleet totals are not one airport gauge reading.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original daily sleet/ice occurrence timeline against surface temperature and regional travel impacts

reviews.title_after: The Groundhog Day tornado outbreak tears across central Florida
reviews.display_location: Lake and Volusia counties, central Florida
reviews.evidence_independence: NOAA/NWS tornado-survey lineage overlapping NCEI; distinct WFO review but not independent damage measurement
reviews.core_fact: NWS Tampa Bay and Melbourne document early-morning February 2, 2007 tornadoes in central Florida; the Turpentine NCEI record is a track segment from the Lake County event, not a separate outbreak.
reviews.unverified_claims: Original NCEI prose describes 'F3'; 2007 was the start of operational Enhanced Fujita ratings. Determine final EF3 path and exact segment before stating the classification; do not aggregate outbreak deaths into the Turpentine segment.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original central Florida surveyed tornado-track map separating the Lady Lake and Paisley/Lake Mack tornadoes

reviews.title_after: Super Tuesday tornado outbreak devastates Tennessee communities
reviews.display_location: Macon County and Tennessee Valley, Tennessee
reviews.evidence_independence: Same NOAA NWS Storm Data and survey-derived counts; NWS Memphis and Nashville have different CWA/outbreak denominators
reviews.core_fact: The February 5–6, 2008 Super Tuesday tornado outbreak included devastating tornadoes in Macon County around Lafayette; the Green Grove Storm Events entry is a local segment, not a separate independent tornado.
reviews.unverified_claims: The Green Grove account's fatalities and injuries are segment- or tornado-specific; do not combine with Union University/Jackson EF4 or total multi-state outbreak figures. Feb 5 local night and Feb 6 overnight must be distinguished.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original tornado-path and local warning-issuance timeline across Macon County and central Tennessee

reviews.title_before: Flood — CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON, Oregon
reviews.title_after: Warm rain on snow triggers the February 1996 Oregon floods
reviews.original_report_location: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON, Oregon
reviews.display_location: Northwestern Oregon, Coast Range and Willamette Basin
reviews.evidence_independence: Cross-agency hydrologic reanalysis/observations supporting the multiday flood; some rainfall descriptions originate from NOAA data
reviews.core_fact: USGS documentation places heavy warm rain and snowmelt across northwestern Oregon around February 6, 1996, when rivers began rising; the NCEI Coast Range zone is only a part of the wider river-flood episode.
reviews.unverified_claims: February 6 marks initial river flooding, NOT the Portland Willamette peak (February 9). USGS dated photo of the Tualatin River is February 10; don't label it a Feb 6 image. Station-specific photos may have item-level public-domain tags that still need checking.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original rain-on-snow mechanism with Feb 6 onset and separately dated USGS streamgage hydrographs

reviews.title_after: A Valentine's Day winter storm spreads across an Arctic Texas
reviews.evidence_independence: NOAA NCEI record and NWS seasonal reanalysis share station observations; not independent measurement of cold minima
reviews.core_fact: The February 14–17, 2021 winter storm arrived amid a prolonged Arctic outbreak across North and Central Texas, and NWS Fort Worth documents widespread statewide winter-weather warnings on February 14.
reviews.unverified_claims: The coldest readings and widespread power impacts followed on later dates. February 11 Fort Worth I-35W pileup preceded the February 14–17 storm; don't conflate them with Valentine's Day snowfall. This NCEI Dallas record is a county-specific cold/wind-chill entry.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Feb 14–17 temperature/snow time series with warning onset and later cold minima separated

reviews.title_after: A violent F3 tornado hits Gallatin during Tennessee's April outbreak
reviews.evidence_independence: Retrospective NWS radar/satellite correction of NCEI historical path; same original survey family, new interpretation not independent tornado observation
reviews.core_fact: NWS Nashville places a destructive April 7, 2006 F3 tornado from Goodlettsville through Hendersonville and Gallatin; NCEI's Gallatin record represents the hard-hit city segment.
reviews.unverified_claims: Use historical F3 Fujita, not EF3. NWS Nashville's 2015 retrospective explicitly revises original NCDC start/end positions and extends a path length estimate; don't copy unreconciled older geometry. Seven direct deaths versus one indirect death are separate categories.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Gallatin-area track showing revised NWS path and identified uncertainty in the historic survey

reviews.title_after: The Bassfield–Soso EF4 becomes Mississippi's widest documented tornado
reviews.evidence_independence: NWS Jackson survey and NCEI county segments share the original investigation; NWS LIX reviews a related but distinct April 12 tornado in adjacent area
reviews.core_fact: NWS Jackson's April 12, 2020 survey identifies the Bassfield–Covington County–Soso–Pachuta EF4 tornado, with an approximately 68-mile track and maximum survey width of 2.25 miles; NCEI Hebron is a reporting segment of that tornado.
reviews.unverified_claims: Do not treat Hebron as another independent tornado. The 2.25-mile maximum width is a surveyed damage extent, NOT continuous EF4 damage at all points or a measured wind field. Distinguish separate Bassfield-area EF4 storms that Easter.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Mississippi five-county EF4 surveyed track with maximum-width section distinct from maximum-rating damage locations

reviews.title_after: Calumet–El Reno–Piedmont EF5 races across central Oklahoma
reviews.display_location: Calumet, El Reno, Piedmont and Guthrie, Oklahoma
reviews.evidence_independence: Same NOAA/NCEI tornado-survey origins; original Oklahoma Mesonet and mobile-radar measurements supplement track evidence
reviews.core_fact: NWS Norman documents the May 24, 2011 Calumet–El Reno–Piedmont–Guthrie EF5 tornado; NCEI Calumet is the opening portion of this single long-track tornado, not its own EF5.
reviews.unverified_claims: Do not confuse the May 24 2011 EF5 with the separate May 31 2013 El Reno tornado. The Oklahoma Mesonet 151-mph gust is a station observation and not equal to the EF5 damage-estimated peak wind; radar measurements were at separate heights.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original surveyed EF5 path plus Oklahoma Mesonet wind trace with clear station/time and EF5-damage labels

reviews.title_after: An EF3 tornado cuts through Perryton in the Texas Panhandle
reviews.evidence_independence: NCEI event and NWS Amarillo office storm survey are the same survey family; not a second independently measured tornado
reviews.core_fact: NWS Amarillo documents an EF3 tornado crossing Perryton on June 15, 2023, during a line of storms with embedded supercells and other small tornadoes nearby.
reviews.unverified_claims: Keep the Perryton EF3 separate from landspout tornadoes near the parent supercell and from the Higgins/Oklahoma track. EF3 maximum is damage based; the number of fatalities must be scoped to the Perryton tornado and updated from final reports.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Perryton track over town with separate landspout markers, storm evolution and radar timestamps

reviews.title_after: Training storms begin the deadliest eastern Kentucky flood phase
reviews.display_location: Knott, Perry, Breathitt and adjacent eastern Kentucky counties
reviews.evidence_independence: Same NOAA rainfall/radar reports as NCEI; USGS field response confirms inundation but not individual radar estimates
reviews.core_fact: NWS Jackson documents renewed training thunderstorms beginning the evening of July 27, 2022, with the peak of eastern Kentucky's flash-flood impacts overnight into July 28; the NCEI Fisty entry describes local Knott County impacts.
reviews.unverified_claims: Do not state the July 27 date as the entire flood's peak or call July 28 Fisty rescues 'on July 27.' NWS Stage IV storm totals cover July 25–30, not a single day; radar totals and human reports have different uncertainty.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original July 27 evening to July 28 morning warning/rainfall timeline, with Fisty impacts marked on their actual dates

reviews.title_after: Downslope winds fuel Lahaina's catastrophic Maui wildfire
reviews.corroborating_publisher: NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office
reviews.evidence_independence: NASA weather reanalysis and NOAA fire incident narrative use overlapping observing networks, but the NASA terrain-flow interpretation is a separate analysis
reviews.core_fact: NASA documents strong terrain-accelerated downslope winds and dry conditions over western Maui on August 8, 2023, when fires spread catastrophically in Lahaina; an August 8 evening Landsat observation separately confirms active burning.
reviews.unverified_claims: Do not imply that Hurricane Dora directly struck Maui; its distant circulation and Pacific high shaped the pressure gradient, alongside terrain effects. NASA modeled downslope wind effects are not direct anemometer observations. Fire ignition cause is not established by wind conditions.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original transect illustrating Puʻu Kukui downslope acceleration and timestamped August 8 fire detection from Earth observation

reviews.title_after: Hurricane Charley rapidly intensifies before striking southwest Florida
reviews.evidence_independence: NHC operational advisory and NCEI/NWS storm summaries are same NOAA-family sources; they do not represent independent wind observations
reviews.core_fact: NHC's August 13, 2004 advisory described Hurricane Charley making landfall as a Category 4 hurricane near Charlotte Harbor, causing major impacts to the Punta Gorda/Port Charlotte area.
reviews.unverified_claims: Landfall location/clock may be described as Cayo Costa, near Charlotte Harbor or west of Punta Gorda depending on source chronology; preserve the operational/advisory date and verify best-track later. Do not equate 145–150-mph estimated maximum sustained wind with a measured point gust. NCEI Charlotte county is a regional segment.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original NHC track and before-landfall intensity timeline with radar and hurricane warnings dated August 13

reviews.title_after: A record flash flood sends a fast-moving wave through Waverly, Tennessee
reviews.display_location: Waverly and Trace Creek, Humphreys County, Tennessee
reviews.evidence_independence: Cross-institution contemporaneous emergency report independently documents dated rescues/road impacts; NCEI's rainfall/gauge/warning estimates remain NOAA-derived
reviews.core_fact: Tennessee's emergency management agency documented widespread catastrophic central Tennessee flooding and rescue operations on August 21, 2021, consistent with the NCEI Pigeon Roost reporting segment in the Waverly/Trace Creek disaster.
reviews.unverified_claims: The spectacular 10-minute flood rise in NCEI's narrative requires separate verification from gauge/time-stamped eyewitness evidence; don't present it as instrument-measured. Rainfall/death totals are for different geographic/time windows and must be explicitly scoped.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Trace Creek catchment and flash-flood warning timeline with verified dated impacts; any 10-minute rise labeled unverified

reviews.title_after: Slow-moving tropical rain system floods southeast Louisiana
reviews.display_location: Baton Rouge, Amite basin and southeast Louisiana
reviews.evidence_independence: NWS meteorological account plus USGS independent streamgage/flood-stage observations; rainfall input and river forecast systems share some data
reviews.core_fact: NWS New Orleans/Baton Rouge documents intense rainfall during August 11–13, 2016; USGS says its some streamgages first passed flood stage August 13, as catastrophic flooding unfolded.
reviews.unverified_claims: Several rivers did not crest until Aug14 or later; the 20–30-inch multi-day rainfall cannot be described as a single Aug13 daily measurement. Source gauge-specific crest and date are required.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original three-day rain/watershed timeline and USGS dated gauge stages; no reused imagery without rights approval

reviews.title_after: Thunderstorm winds trigger the Indiana State Fair stage collapse
reviews.evidence_independence: Indiana state history independently chronicles date and wind-related collapse; NWS Indianapolis archives August13 severe weather but historical case link is no longer served
reviews.core_fact: The Indiana state history records that on August 13, 2011 thunderstorm wind gusts caused a stage collapse at the Indianapolis fairgrounds; NWS Indianapolis's historical index lists severe storms on the same date.
reviews.unverified_claims: Weather.gov/ind/aug132011severe now returns 404. Do not use unavailable old NWS imagery. Exact on-site gusts are estimated, not necessarily measured. Engineering/structural liability not determined by meteorological reports alone.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original storm-warning clock and annotated gust observations around Indianapolis; no accident imagery without asset permission
